investigations.name: annealing
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 2+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=2, J_dd=2, J_ld=2, J_lM=8, J_dM=8 (gamma_ld=+0, gamma_lM=+7, gamma_dM=+7); T=0.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_light. Figures reproduced: Fig 2, Fig 3.
investigations.title: Annealing convergence
investigations.objective: Does the pattern's topology (<n>, moments) converge within a few MCS of T=0 annealing, as in Glazier-Graner Fig 2-3?
investigations.claim: Bulk <n> converges to ~5.97 within ~2 MCS with total<bulk, reproducing Fig 2; cell walls compact by 2-20 MCS (Fig 3).

investigations.name: cell_sorting
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 12+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=14, J_dd=2, J_ld=11, J_lM=16, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+3, gamma_lM=+9, gamma_dM=+15); T=10.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 12, Fig 13, Fig 14, Fig 15, Fig 16, Table II, Table III.
investigations.title: Cell sorting
investigations.objective: Does differential adhesion (gamma_dM>gamma_lM>gamma_ld>0) sort a random mix into dark-inside / light-monolayer, as observed by Armstrong and Steinberg?
investigations.claim: Complete cell sorting: dark cells cluster internally beneath a light monolayer; heterotypic contact falls while light-medium contact rises, reproducing Figs 12-16 and Tables II-III.

investigations.name: checkerboard
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 7+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=10, J_dd=8, J_ld=6, J_lM=12, J_dM=12 (gamma_ld=-3, gamma_lM=+7, gamma_dM=+8); T=10.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 7, Fig 8, Fig 9, Table I.
investigations.title: Checkerboard (negative surface tension)
investigations.objective: Does a negative light-dark surface tension (gamma_ld=-3) drive intermixing into a checkerboard instead of sorting?
investigations.claim: gamma_ld<0 yields a defect-ridden checkerboard with dominant light-dark contact and two transitions (~T=0 freeze, ~T=15 mixing), matching Figs 7-9 and Table I.

investigations.name: dispersal_no_separate
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 27+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=14, J_dd=2, J_ld=29, J_lM=16, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+21, gamma_lM=+9, gamma_dM=+15); T=5.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 27.
investigations.title: Dispersal - clusters do not separate
investigations.objective: At gamma_ld=21, do light/dark clusters stay attached (extreme partial sorting) rather than fully separate?
investigations.claim: Clusters remain attached, an extreme partial-sorting case just below the separation threshold (Fig 27).

investigations.name: dispersal_separate
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 26+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=14, J_dd=2, J_ld=35, J_lM=16, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+27, gamma_lM=+9, gamma_dM=+15); T=5.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 26.
investigations.title: Dispersal - clusters separate
investigations.objective: Does a very high heterotypic tension (gamma_ld=27) make light and dark clusters fully separate?
investigations.claim: Light and dark clusters separate completely; a few isolated dark cells occur (Fig 26).

investigations.name: dispersal_sloughing
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 25+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=14, J_dd=4, J_ld=11, J_lM=2, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+2, gamma_lM=-5, gamma_dM=+14); T=5.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 25.
investigations.title: Dispersal - light-cell sloughing
investigations.objective: Does a negative light-Medium tension (gamma_lM=-5) make light cells slough off and disperse into the medium?
investigations.claim: Light cells disperse as isolated cells into the medium while dark cells remain compact and round (Fig 25).

investigations.name: engulfment
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 18+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=14, J_dd=2, J_ld=11, J_lM=16, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+3, gamma_lM=+9, gamma_dM=+15); T=10.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: half_split. Figures reproduced: Fig 18, Fig 19.
investigations.title: Engulfment
investigations.objective: Does an initially half-light/half-dark aggregate engulf to the same sorted configuration as the random-IC sort?
investigations.claim: Light cells engulf the dark mass and the final state matches the random-IC sort, confirming initial-condition independence (Figs 18-19).

investigations.name: epithelial-fate
investigations.description:
Increment 4 of the influenza-sego2022 capability ladder: adds infected
death (I->D, a simplified flat rate) and the cellularized Allee effect
(H->D death / D->H recovery, both driven by local epithelial contact
geometry and gated by per-cell resistance) on top of the Increment-2/3
infection + IFN-resistance mechanism. No chemokine/IL-10 fields, no
immune cells (macrophage/NK/CD8+ T), no NK/CD8 contact-killing, and no
APC-driven global IFN amplification -- those arrive in later increments.
The death-rate coefficient (`mu_i_per_mcs`) and the Allee rate coefficient
(`b_h`) plus threshold (`srf_threshold`) are taken from the CC3D
ViralInfectionVTM source (see `pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/params.yaml`'s
`cell_death:` and `allee:` blocks); `srf_total`/`srf_uninfected` are
restricted to epithelial (H/I/D) neighbor contact, excluding MEDIUM,
matching the source's `ec_list` filter (a design decision recorded in
task-4.3-report.md, since it diverges from an earlier brief's looser
"sum over all neighbor types" phrasing).
investigations.title: Epithelial death & Allee recovery
investigations.objective:
Layered on the validated Increment-2/3 virus field + infection + IFN-
resistance path: does wiring ALL epithelial fates together -- infection
(H->I), infected death (I->D), and the cellularized Allee effect (H->D
death / D->H recovery, both gated by local contact geometry and
per-cell resistance) -- produce a coherent cell-fate lifecycle where a
dead lesion grows via H->I->D and dead cells surrounded by healthy
tissue recover, while dead cells surrounded by dying tissue do not?
investigations.claim:
Wiring infection, infected death, and the cellularized Allee effect
together produces a coherent, population-conserving epithelial-fate
lifecycle: a dead lesion grows, and dead cells surrounded by healthy
tissue recover while those surrounded by dying tissue never do. This
validates the mechanism only, not a reproduction of Sego et al. 2022's
figure targets. Direct Allee death is honestly reported as rare at this
scale, verified genuine rather than a wiring bug.

investigations.name: epithelial-sheet-baseline
investigations.description:
Increment 1 of the influenza-sego2022 capability ladder: the bare
confluent epithelial sheet, no virus field, no infection, no immune
cells. A uniform grid of 5x5-site (10 um) type-H cells tiles the patch;
adhesion is the source-literal CC3D value (H-H=5.0, H-medium=25.0,
CONTROLLER OVERRIDE vs the CC3D-typical 4.0/16.0 — see
`pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/sheet.py`). This study validates that the
substrate is mechanically sound (confluent, stable target volume) and
computationally fast enough — it does NOT attempt, and is not scored
against, any biological reproduction target. The live-demo composite here
runs a small 0.1mm/100-cell patch for a fast dashboard "run baseline";
the 1mm^2/10000-cell throughput characterization is a separate perf test
(`tests/test_influenza_perf.py`, Task 1.3), not re-run live by this
composite.
investigations.title: Epithelial sheet baseline
investigations.objective:
Does the CPM engine hold a confluent, source-literal-adhesion epithelial
sheet stable (no gaps, no vanished cells) at 1 mm^2 paper scale, and does
it step fast enough (Rust engine, `step_parallel`) for the eventual
2-week/~20160-MCS capstone run to be computationally feasible?
investigations.claim:
The confluent epithelial-only sheet is geometrically stable (mean cell
volume ~25 sites, none vanished) and the Rust CPM engine steps the full
1mm^2 lattice at ~406-422 MCS/s, far above the throughput needed to make
the eventual 2-week capstone run computationally tractable. This is a
substrate-readiness claim, not a biological-reproduction claim.

investigations.name: global-coupling
investigations.description:
Increment 8 of the influenza-sego2022 capability ladder: adds the
Price (2015)-derived global (whole-organ) immune ODE compartment,
integrated once per MCS and coupled BIDIRECTIONALLY to the spatial CPM
patch built up across Increments 1-7. This is the increment that
resolves the three mechanisms carried as documented stubs since
Increments 5-7 — the static `sig_1` secretion-scale constant
(Increment 6), the absent chemokine/APC-driven recruitment dynamics
(fixed populations, Increments 5-7), and the LOCAL-only NK/CD8
cytotoxic-killing term (Increment 7, no well-mixed nearby-population
contribution) — into dynamic, ODE-driven mechanisms. Each is verified
individually correct and source-faithful (the Michaelis secretion form,
the CD8-no-baseline recruitment asymmetry, the nearby-killing wiring via
a documented test seam). This study's central, deliberately UN-hidden
contribution is reporting — not concealing — that at this driver's small
reduced-scale default (tiny eta ~1.4e-4), none of the three mechanisms'
MAGNITUDES yet reconcile with the values they replaced or need to
produce an observable effect within a feasible step budget: this is a
field-vs-ODE unit-scale calibration gap, the same category of finding
already recorded for macrophage/NK/CD8 chemotaxis in Increments 5/7, now
propagating into the ODE-coupling layer. No Figs 3B/5/7 quantitative
reproduction claim is made here — that is Increment 9 (the capstone),
which needs this study's calibration gaps resolved first.
investigations.title: Global Price-2015 ODE coupling
investigations.objective:
Coupling the Price (2015)-derived global immune ODE (10 systemic
species) bidirectionally to the spatial CPM patch — spatial aggregates
feeding the ODE each MCS, the freshly-integrated ODE state (TNF, APC)
feeding back into spatial secretion regulation and recruitment — do the
three mechanisms carried as documented stubs since Increments 5-7
(static sig_1, absent recruitment, LOCAL-only cytotoxic killing) now
resolve into DYNAMIC, ODE-driven mechanisms that are individually
correct and source-faithful, and — the honest question this study
exists to surface — do the resulting coupling MAGNITUDES already
reconcile at this reduced-scale patch, or is the wiring correct while
the field-vs-ODE unit scales still need Increment-9 calibration?
investigations.claim:
The hybrid global immune ODE integrates stably each step and couples
bidirectionally with the spatial model, resolving three previously-
stubbed mechanisms — dynamic IL-10/chemokine signaling, ODE-driven
recruitment, and a nearby-population killing term — each individually
verified correct. At this reduced-scale patch, none of these mechanisms'
magnitudes yet reconcile with the values replaced or reach an observable
effect: a field-versus-ODE unit-scale calibration gap, reported honestly
and deferred rather than tuned away.

investigations.name: global_equilibration
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 4+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=2, J_dd=2, J_ld=2, J_lM=8, J_dM=8 (gamma_ld=+0, gamma_lM=+7, gamma_dM=+7); T=5.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: brick_equilibrate. Figures reproduced: Fig 4, Fig 5.
investigations.title: Global pattern equilibration
investigations.objective: Does a rectangular brick tiling relax into a rounded, topologically-equilibrated aggregate at T=5?
investigations.claim: The tiling rounds into a 1012-cell disk with <n>~6.0, mu2~0.69, matching Fig 4b; statistics stable after ~400 MCS (Fig 5).

investigations.name: ifn-resistance
investigations.description:
Increment 3 of the influenza-sego2022 capability ladder: adds ONE new
diffusible field (type-I IFN) and ONE new per-cell state computation
(resistance, from local IFN) that gates the Increment-2 virus-secretion
rate. No death/recovery, no Allee effect, no IL-10 cross-talk, no immune
cells, and no APC-driven global IFN amplification — those arrive in later
increments. The IFN field's diffusion/decay/secretion constants and the
resistance formula's `a_rf` constant are taken from the CC3D
ViralInfectionVTM source (see `pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/params.yaml`'s
`ifn:` and `resistance:` blocks); the resistance formula matches the
source's stored convention (`resist = f_bar/(a_rf+f_bar)`, a plain
Hill/saturation function), NOT the paper's printed form
(`rho = 1 - f_bar'/(theta*a_f+f_bar')`) — every source consumer applies
`(1-resist_source)` wherever the paper's rho appears protectively, which
is exactly how `run_virus_infection_with_ifn` uses it.
investigations.title: Type-I IFN field & cellular resistance
investigations.objective:
Layered on the validated Increment-2 virus field + infection transition:
does a diffusing type-I IFN field, converted per-cell into a resistance
scalar (source formula `resist = f_bar/(a_rf+f_bar)`), gate an infected
cell's virus secretion by `(1-resist)` strongly enough to measurably
REDUCE infection spread and total virus versus the same run with no IFN
(Increment 2's path, unchanged)?
investigations.claim:
A type-I IFN field, converted per-cell into a resistance scalar, gates
virus secretion and roughly halves total virus versus an identical
no-IFN run — the study's primary, robust evidence. Infected-cell count
moves the same protective direction but more weakly, becoming meaningful
only later in the run. This validates the mechanism only; it is not a
claim that Sego et al. 2022's quantitative figure targets are met, which
remains pending.

investigations.name: immune-response
investigations.description:
Consolidated immune-response scene at tissue scale: a confluent ~900-cell
epithelial sheet (30x30 cells) seeded with a 12-cell infected patch, with 20
macrophages + 20 NK + 20 CD8+ T cells placed off the sheet. The immune cells
chemotax up the macrophage-released chemokine field toward the infection and
cluster against the sheet. This subsumes the three earlier increment demos
(macrophage-response = chemotaxis, signaling-fields = chemokine/IL-10 field,
cytotoxic-killing = NK/CD8 cytotoxicity), which are removed in favour of this
single representative-scale study. Driver: run_cytotoxic_response
(epithelial_cells_per_side=30, n_infected=12, n_macrophages/n_nk/n_cd8=20,
margin_sites=6, separation_sites=2, steps=60, seed=17).
investigations.title: Immune response at tissue scale
investigations.objective:
Do the innate/adaptive immune mechanisms — macrophage chemotaxis, the
macrophage-released chemokine/IL-10 signalling field, and NK/CD8 cytotoxic
localisation — compose into a coherent immune response at a REPRESENTATIVE
tissue scale (~900-cell epithelial sheet), rather than only in the tiny
(~10-cell) single-mechanism unit-tests?
investigations.claim:
The immune mechanisms (macrophage/NK/CD8 chemotaxis + chemokine signalling)
compose and localise toward infection at tissue scale. Contact-killing at full
scale remains the documented field-magnitude calibration gap (quantified in the
capstone) -- this is a MECHANISM result, not a Fig-3B/5/7 reproduction claim.

investigations.name: parameter-provenance
investigations.description:
Increment 0 of the influenza-sego2022 investigation. This study documents,
rather than simulates: it cites the parameter authority
(pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/params.yaml), the CC3D-source acquisition and
transcription docs (docs/cc3d-reference/sego2022-source-notes.md and
sego2022-parameters.md), and the digitized figure targets
(pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/targets/{fig3b,fig5,fig7}.json). It reference the
bibliography entry sego2022influenza (workspace/references/papers.bib) for
the paper itself. No composite, run, or simulated observable exists in this
study — those begin at Increment 1 (epithelial-sheet-baseline).
investigations.title: Parameter provenance & digitized Fig 3B/5/7 targets
investigations.objective:
What is the authoritative, cited parameter set for reproducing Sego et al.
2022's cellularized influenza model, and where does that authority (the
CC3D ViralInfectionVTM source) disagree with the paper's own printed
tables?
investigations.claim:
The parameter authority for the influenza-sego2022 investigation is
established and cited: params.yaml is sourced from the CC3D
ViralInfectionVTM package and the paper's Tables 1-4, with every value
traceable to one or the other, and figure-target acceptance bands exist for
Figs 3B, 5, 7. This is a claim of DOCUMENTATION COMPLETENESS, not of
reproduction — no simulation has been run against these targets.

investigations.name: partial_sorting
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 22+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=11, J_dd=2, J_ld=14, J_lM=16, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+7.5, gamma_lM=+10.5, gamma_dM=+15); T=5.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 22, Fig 23, Fig 24.
investigations.title: Partial cell sorting
investigations.objective: Does violating the Young condition (large gamma_ld=7.5) stall sorting at a partially-sorted, trapped state?
investigations.claim: Sorting stalls partial: no light monolayer forms and clusters trap inclusions, markedly slower than normal sorting (Figs 22-24).

investigations.name: position_reversal
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 20+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=14, J_dd=2, J_ld=11, J_lM=30, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+3, gamma_lM=+23, gamma_dM=+15); T=10.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 20, Fig 21.
investigations.title: Position reversal
investigations.objective: Does raising the light-Medium tension (gamma_lM=23) reverse the sorting so dark cells end up outside?
investigations.claim: Dark cells sort OUTWARD, surrounding the light cells, the reversed pattern predicted for gamma_lM>gamma_dM (Figs 20-21).

investigations.name: recruitment-adaptive
investigations.description:
This is the LOCKED CONTRACT study for the adaptive rung of the
recruitment-model-building faithful mechanism ladder (static_lambda ->
hill_occupancy -> adaptive_receptor). The ladder is built and calibrated:
static recruits at every background (it is not receptor-mediated, so the
background cancels out of the chemotaxis bias exactly); hill_occupancy
recruits at low background but collapses once a high uniform background
saturates receptor occupancy on both sides of the local gradient; and
adaptive_receptor rescues recruitment at high background by re-centering
its effective kd on the locally sensed mean every SAMPLE-step increment,
so it detects the FOLD CHANGE (the rise) in local concentration rather than
its absolute level. This study authors the behavior_tests that make "the
adaptive model works" falsifiable and locked BEFORE the loop is driven
against it: recruitment at low background, recruitment at high background
(the discriminating test -- only the adaptive mechanism passes; hill
collapses to 0), and receptor gating (blocking the response abolishes
recruitment for both receptor-gated mechanisms, but NOT for the
non-receptor-mediated static mechanism, which is the discriminating
knockout the loop must climb past). `conditions.baseline.composite`
points at the real, registered base recruitment world
(pbg_cpm_studies.composites.chemotaxis.recruitment -- source secretion +
responder chemotaxis, shared by all three ladder mechanisms); the
adaptive_receptor mechanism itself (kd/hill/epsilon) is what the loop
INSTALLS on top of that base world, documented under
`conditions.model_settings` rather than as baseline params, since it
directly manipulates the Rust CPM engine's chemotaxis-occupancy API
(world.set_chemotaxis_occupancy + a per-increment adaptation update)
rather than being its own registered @composite_generator. The actual
runner the loop drives is
mechanisms.simulate_condition("adaptive_receptor", condition, seeds,
steps) (see key_assumptions / model_change).
investigations.title: Adaptive receptor recruitment: fold-change detection across background cue levels
investigations.objective:
Across a range of background cue levels (fold_change_detection), does an
adaptive receptor mechanism keep recruiting responders to a rising
source cue where a fixed-kd mechanism saturates and collapses?
investigations.claim:
A receptor mechanism that adapts its half-occupancy set-point to the
locally sensed background (fold-change detection) recruits responders
across a RANGE of background cue levels where a fixed-kd mechanism
saturates and fails: measured recruitment_index at low_bg is 0.82
(adaptive) vs 0.58 (hill); at high_bg it is ~0.56 (adaptive, mean over 12
seeds) vs 0.00 (hill, deterministic collapse). Blocking the receptor-gated
response abolishes recruitment for both (0.00), while the non-receptor
static mechanism ignores the block (0.72) -- the discriminating control
that isolates receptor-mediated gating as the necessary cause.

investigations.name: recruitment-adversarial
investigations.description:
The adversarial / negative-control arm. Responders are fully competent (lambda=14)
but there is no cue (secretion rate 0), so no gradient forms. A trustworthy
recruitment claim must FAIL to fire here — the metric passes by rejecting a system
that should not qualify. This closes the causal logic: recruitment requires BOTH a
cue AND a response, and neither alone suffices.
investigations.title: Control: no cue, no recruitment
investigations.objective:
If competent responders are placed with NO cue secreted, does the metric
correctly report no recruitment (rather than a spurious signal)?
investigations.claim:
Without a cue, competent responders are not recruited: the recruitment index
stays at 0. The metric does not produce a false-positive recruitment signal.

investigations.name: recruitment-baseline
investigations.description:
The anchoring positive condition of the chemotactic-recruitment slice. Type-1
source cells secrete field C (d=0.22, decay=0.001); type-2 responders start ~33 px
away and chemotax up the gradient with strength lambda=14. This is the native
viva-cpm realization of the biological claim "a secreted cue recruits responder
cells", and the ground-truth study the Biological Claim Layer compiler must
reproduce.
investigations.title: Baseline: cue + response recruits
investigations.objective:
When source cells secrete a diffusible cue and responder cells carry a
competent chemotactic response, do responders migrate up the gradient and
accumulate at the source?
investigations.claim:
Responders climb the secreted gradient and are recruited to the source: the
recruitment index rises from 0 to a plateau of ~0.67-0.83 (mean approach 0.61).

investigations.name: recruitment-inhibited
investigations.description:
The intervention arm of the slice. The world is identical to the baseline except
the responder chemotaxis lambda is set to 0 — the CPM analogue of pharmacologically
blocking the receptor/response while the cue is unchanged. This is the claim
layer's "intervention on the response" made concrete: same cue, blocked response.
investigations.title: Intervention: block the response
investigations.objective:
If the chemotactic response is blocked (lambda -> 0) while the cue is still
secreted, is recruitment abolished?
investigations.claim:
Blocking the chemotactic response abolishes recruitment: the recruitment index
stays at 0 (mean approach ~0), despite the cue being present.

investigations.name: recruitment-receptor-baseline
investigations.description:
The receptor-level realization of the chemotactic-recruitment claim. Where
recruitment-baseline gives every responder a hardcoded, always-on
chemotactic bias, this study makes the response emergent: each responder
carries a per-cell ReceptorSubcell that reads the local cue concentration
and computes fractional receptor occupancy via a Hill relation (kd, hill,
conc_scale, activate_occupancy). Only once occupancy crosses threshold does
a responder flip from naive (type 2, non-chemotaxing) to activated (type 3,
chemotaxing) -- see
pbg_cpm_studies.composites.chemotaxis_receptor.recruitment_receptor. The
receptor's Kd is not a free-fit parameter: it is the CXCL8 monomer-CXCR1
affinity reported in Nasser et al. 2009 (2.9 nM), so activation is
calibrated to a real receptor-ligand pair rather than an arbitrary lambda.
The Kd calibration is recorded as a parameter (model_settings below), not
as a literature_target on the recruitment-index test -- recruitment index
is a 0-1 fraction, and a Kd-valued target on that test would corrupt any
divergence_factor computed from it.
investigations.title: Receptor realization: cue + receptor-gated response recruits
investigations.objective:
Does a receptor-level realization of chemotactic recruitment -- where each
responder activates from naive to chemotaxing only once its per-cell
receptor-occupancy Hill relation crosses threshold -- reproduce the
baseline recruitment claim, using a cited receptor Kd instead of a
hand-tuned chemotaxis strength?
investigations.claim:
Cue + receptor-gated response recruits: across 5 seeds the final
recruitment index is 0.5667 (95% CI 0.3451-0.7882), above the 0.5 pass
threshold, with responder activation gated by a receptor Kd cited to
Nasser 2009 rather than a hand-tuned chemotaxis strength.

investigations.name: recruitment-receptor-blocked
investigations.description:
The intervention arm of the receptor-level realization, paired with
recruitment-receptor-baseline. The world and receptor wiring are identical
to the baseline -- same cue, same per-cell ReceptorSubcell computing Hill
occupancy against the same cited Kd (2.9 nM, Nasser et al. 2009) -- except
the activated type's chemotaxis lambda is forced to 0 in
chemotaxis_receptor.build_receptor_spec, the receptor-realization analogue
of pharmacologically blocking the response downstream of receptor binding.
As in the baseline, the Kd is recorded as a calibrated parameter
(model_settings below), not as a literature_target on the recruitment-index
test.
investigations.title: Receptor realization: blocking the response abolishes recruitment
investigations.objective:
In the receptor-level realization, if the activated response is forced off
(blocked=True, zeroing the activated-type chemotaxis lambda even for cells
that cross the receptor-occupancy activation threshold) while the cue is
still secreted, is recruitment abolished?
investigations.claim:
Blocking the response downstream of receptor activation abolishes
recruitment: the final recruitment index is 0.0667 (95% CI 0.0-0.1467),
below the 0.1 pass threshold, despite the cue being present and receptors
still able to bind ligand.

investigations.name: repro-fig3b
investigations.description:
Increment 9 Task 9.2 (part of the capstone reproduction ladder):
`run.repro_fig3b` is the ensemble-and-band-comparison driver for the
Sego-2022 Fig-3B scenario, built on top of Task 9.1's `run.
run_full_model` (every mechanism subsystem from Increments 0-8 assembled
into one source-ordered per-MCS loop) and Task 9.0's `bands` acceptance-
band harness (`targets/fig3b.json`, digitized from the paper's Fig. 3B).
This task WIRES the ensemble machinery and EVALUATES it -- it explicitly
does NOT attempt the paper-scale 50-replica, 35x35-cell, ~3.5-day ensemble
needed to actually claim Fig-3B reproduction; that run is deferred to the
Mac-mini Phase-B follow-up (documented in `repro_fig3b`'s own docstring).
The reduced-scale config this task's fast pytest test uses (`replicas=2,
cells_per_side=15, steps=20`) is run directly here and its actual
`band_eval` result reported honestly: 0 of 12 observables are in-band at
every digitized checkpoint, driven by population-scale (225 vs. 1225
cells) and run-duration (~0.09 vs. up to 3.5 simulated days) mismatch --
not by tuning any constant, and `targets/fig3b.json` is not edited.
investigations.title: Reproduction — Fig 3B (time series vs ODE)
investigations.objective:
With every mechanism subsystem from Increments 0-8 wired into ONE
per-MCS loop (`run.run_full_model`, Task 9.1), does running that model
as a seeded ensemble over the Sego-2022 Fig-3B scenario (5% initial
infection, 0.3 mm / 1225-cell patch) and comparing the ensemble mean to
the digitized Fig-3B acceptance bands (`targets/fig3b.json`,
`bands.evaluate_study`) show the model landing in-band -- and, the
honest question this task exists to surface, does a REDUCED-scale
ensemble (small population, few replicas, short duration -- the only
scale a fast CI test can afford) tell us anything meaningful about
fidelity, or does it mostly measure population-scale and run-duration
mismatch rather than mechanism correctness?
investigations.claim:
`repro_fig3b` correctly assembles a seeded ensemble of the full model
over the Fig-3B scenario and evaluates it against the digitized
acceptance bands, producing a well-formed result. Fig-3B is not
reproduced at the reduced scale a fast test affords: none of the twelve
observables land in-band at every checkpoint, a scale-and-duration
mismatch rather than evidence of a mechanism defect. A paper-scale
ensemble is required before any reproduction verdict.

investigations.name: repro-fig5-viral-load
investigations.description:
Increment 9 Task 9.3 (part of the capstone reproduction ladder):
`run.repro_fig5` is the per-load viral-load-sweep ensemble driver for the
Sego-2022 Fig-5 scenario family, built on top of Task 9.1's `run.
run_full_model` (every mechanism subsystem from Increments 0-8 assembled
into one source-ordered per-MCS loop), Task 9.0's `bands` acceptance-band
harness, and the load-bearing SCENARIO-GROUPING GUARD the Task-9.0 review
called out: `targets/fig5.json`'s observable lists interleave all 5
viral-load scenarios in one flat list per observable, tagged by
`viral_load_multiplier`, so evaluating a single load's model run against
the WHOLE unfiltered list would silently average its comparison against
every other load's band too. `_fig5_target_subset` filters to just that
load's tagged entries (raising loudly, not falling back silently, if a
requested load has no matches) before `_evaluate_fig5_subset` runs
`bands.series_in_band`'s containment check. This task WIRES the sweep
machinery and EVALUATES it -- it explicitly does NOT attempt the
paper-scale 50-replica, all-5-load, 35x35-cell, ~15-day ensemble needed
to actually claim Fig-5 reproduction; that run is deferred to the
Mac-mini Phase-B follow-up (documented in `repro_fig5`'s own docstring,
including the corrected `steps≈3086` for the full 15-day window at
`mcs_per_step=7, s_per_mcs=60` -- NOT the `steps≈2880`/2-day figure a
prior task mistakenly used for this figure). The reduced-scale config
this task's fast pytest test uses (`loads=(1,10000), replicas=1,
cells_per_side=12, steps=15`) is run directly here and its actual
`band_eval` result reported honestly: both loads fail per-load band
containment, but the monotone dose-response direction the paper's own
Fig-5 narrative depends on holds cleanly at this reduced scale.
investigations.title: Reproduction — Fig 5 (viral-load sweep)
investigations.objective:
With every mechanism subsystem from Increments 0-8 wired into ONE
per-MCS loop (`run.run_full_model`, Task 9.1), does sweeping that model
over Sego-2022 Fig-5's five initial-viral-load scenarios (1x, 10x, 100x,
1000x, 10000x the ODE-calibrated dose, uniform virus-field IC, zero
pre-infected cells) reproduce the paper's central Fig-5 finding -- a
MONOTONE, threshold-like dose-response in which the spatial model stays
non-lethal for multipliers up to 1000x and trends toward lethal
(near-total uninfected-cell loss) only near 10000x -- and, honestly,
does a REDUCED-scale sweep (few loads/replicas, a short population and
run duration, the only scale a fast CI test can afford) show the
monotone DIRECTION even though it cannot match the digitized bands'
absolute magnitudes at paper scale?
investigations.claim:
`repro_fig5` is wired correctly: it sweeps a seeded ensemble of the full
model across Fig-5's viral-load scenarios and evaluates each load
against only its own acceptance-band subset. This study does not claim
Fig-5 is reproduced — at reduced population and run duration, per-load
band containment fails, though the monotone dose-response direction
(higher initial viral load, fewer surviving uninfected cells) holds. A
paper-scale ensemble is required before any reproduction verdict.

investigations.name: repro-fig7-infection-fraction
investigations.description:
Increment 9 Task 9.4 (the final task of the capstone reproduction ladder):
`run.repro_fig7` is the per-fraction infection-fraction-sweep ensemble
driver for the Sego-2022 Fig-7 scenario family, built on top of Task
9.1's `run.run_full_model` (every mechanism subsystem from Increments 0-8
assembled into one source-ordered per-MCS loop), Task 9.0's `bands`
acceptance-band harness, and Task 9.3's SCENARIO-GROUPING GUARD, now
generalized (DRY, per the brief's stated preference and this task's
verification that doing so preserves fig5's exact prior behavior) into a
shared `_scenario_target_subset`/`_evaluate_scenario_subset` pair used by
BOTH `_fig5_target_subset`/`_evaluate_fig5_subset` and this task's new
`_fig7_target_subset`/`_evaluate_fig7_subset`: `targets/fig7.json`'s
observable lists interleave all 4 initial-infection-fraction scenarios in
one flat list per observable, tagged by `initial_infection_fraction`, so
evaluating a single fraction's model run against the WHOLE unfiltered
list would silently average its comparison against every other
fraction's band too. This task WIRES the sweep machinery, EVALUATES it,
and closes a test-coverage gap the Task-9.3 review flagged (the guard was
only verified interactively, not in pytest) by adding a dedicated fast
unit test for the filter-and-raise behavior. It explicitly does NOT
attempt the paper-scale 20-replica, all-4-fraction, 35x35-cell, ~15-day
ensemble needed to actually claim Fig-7 reproduction; that run is
deferred to the Mac-mini Phase-B follow-up (documented in `repro_fig7`'s
own docstring, following `repro_fig5`'s corrected `steps≈3086` derivation
for the full 15-day window at `mcs_per_step=7, s_per_mcs=60`, but noting
fig7.json's own `scenario.replicas=20`, not fig5's 50). The reduced-scale
config this task's fast pytest test uses (`fracs=(0.001,0.05), replicas=1,
cells_per_side=12, steps=15`) is run directly here and its actual
`band_eval` result reported honestly: both fractions fail per-fraction
band containment, the monotone dose-response direction holds, and a NEW
reduced-scale artifact is surfaced and reported honestly -- frac=0.001
rounds to ZERO pre-infected cells at `cells_per_side=12`
(`round(0.001*144)=0`), so that point is a degenerate no-infection
control at this population size, not a real exercise of fig7.json's
frac=0.001 scenario.
investigations.title: Reproduction — Fig 7 (infection-fraction sweep)
investigations.objective:
With every mechanism subsystem from Increments 0-8 wired into ONE
per-MCS loop (`run.run_full_model`, Task 9.1), does sweeping that model
over Sego-2022 Fig-7's four initial-infection-fraction scenarios (0.1%,
0.5%, 1%, 5% of the epithelial patch pre-infected, zero initial virus
field) reproduce the paper's central Fig-7/Sec-3.4 finding -- a
threshold-like severity response in which every replica is non-lethal
(the patch recovers) for fraction <=1%, even though the ODE model is
fatal for all of these, while at fraction=5% the spatial model becomes
comparably severe to the ODE model (though some replicas still retain
surviving uninfected cells) -- and, honestly, does a REDUCED-scale sweep
(the only scale a fast CI test can afford) show a consistent (non-more-
surviving-at-higher-fraction) direction even though it cannot match the
digitized bands' absolute magnitudes at paper scale?
investigations.claim:
`repro_fig7` is wired correctly: it sweeps a seeded ensemble of the full
model across Fig-7's infection-fraction scenarios and evaluates each
fraction against only its own acceptance-band subset. Fig-7 is not
reproduced at reduced scale — per-fraction band containment fails, and
the smallest tested fraction degenerates to a no-infection control since
it rounds to zero seeded cells. The monotone dose-response direction
still holds; a paper-scale ensemble is required before reproduction.

investigations.name: vacancy_cavity
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 28+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=14, J_dd=2, J_ld=11, J_lM=16, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+3, gamma_lM=+9, gamma_dM=+15); T=5.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=20.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 28.
investigations.title: Vacancy nucleation (cavity)
investigations.objective: With unequal target areas (A_l=20, A_d=40) and vacancy nucleation allowed, does a light-cell-lined central cavity form?
investigations.claim: A light-cell-lined medium cavity nucleates within the aggregate (Fig 28); reproduced approximately (the paper notes this case is delicate).

investigations.name: virus-field-infection
investigations.description:
Increment 2 of the influenza-sego2022 capability ladder: adds ONE
diffusible field (virus) and ONE new cell-state transition (H -> I,
stochastic, field-driven) on top of the Increment-1 confluent epithelial
sheet. No resistance/IFN, no death/recovery, no immune cells — those
arrive in Increments 3+. The virus field's diffusion coefficient, decay
rate, and target diffusion length (5 cell diameters = 25 lattice sites)
are taken from the CC3D ViralInfectionVTM source (see
`pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/params.yaml`'s `virus:` block); the infection
rate coefficient `g_hv` is likewise source-cited. Two independent
seed-derived RNG streams make the driver run
(`run.run_virus_infection`) fully deterministic: one chooses the initial
lesion, a separate one drives the per-update stochastic transition.
investigations.title: Virus field & stochastic H→I infection
investigations.objective:
Layered on the validated Increment-1 confluent sheet: does a diffusing,
decaying extracellular virus field (source-cited D/decay, target
diffusion length 5 cell diameters = 25 sites) and a stochastic,
virus-driven H -> I infection transition produce LOCAL lesion spread
(new infections cluster near existing infected cells, not uniformly
across the sheet) with population conserved?
investigations.claim:
The extracellular virus field diffuses and decays as specified, and a
seeded lesion of infected cells spreads via a stochastic, virus-driven
healthy-to-infected transition that stays local to existing infection,
with total cell population conserved throughout. This validates the
mechanism only — it is not a claim that any of Sego et al. 2022's
quantitative figure targets are met; that reproduction verdict remains
pending until the capstone increment.
